claims.behaviour: Once the `widget-bare` script has run, `window.almworks.structure.api` is an object with exactly these members besides the class helpers: `ColumnGroup`, `registerColumnGroup` (same function as `ColumnGroup.register`), `ColumnType`, `registerColumnType` (same function as `ColumnType.register`), `ColumnConfigurator`, `Column`, `SpecOption`, `ColumnOption` (same object as `SpecOption`), `registerCoreExtension`, `ItemDetailsProvider`, `registerItemDetailsProvider` and `automationRegistry` (the object also exposed as AMD id `structure/api/AutomationRegistry`).

`window.almworks.structure.api` also carries the class helpers `subClass`, `baseClass`, `isSubClass`, `isInstance`, `addSuper` and `getClassName`. `subClass(name?, superclass, props)` makes a constructor: it calls the superclass as a plain function with the single options argument, copies the non-function entries of `props` onto the new instance, then calls `init(options)` found on the new class's prototype. Function entries of `props` go on the prototype; `prototype._super` is the superclass prototype and `prototype._class` the new class. `name`, when given, must match letters and underscores only, otherwise it throws `invalid function name [<name>]`; a superclass that is not a function throws `bad superclass <value>`; a `props` that is not an object throws `bad props <value>`. `baseClass(name, props)` does the same on a root class whose constructor stores its argument as `this.options`. `isSubClass(a, b)` is true when b is a or derives from it, and true for an empty a; `isInstance(cls, obj)` is true for instances, also through the `_class` chain, and false for an empty obj; `getClassName(obj)` gives the constructor's name; `addSuper(cls, obj)` copies cls's prototype methods, bound to obj, into `obj._super` and returns a function that applies cls to its arguments.

Because `subClass` calls its superclass as a plain function, every public class that companion apps extend (`Column`, `ColumnConfigurator`, `ColumnType`, `SpecOption` and its six option classes, `ColumnGroup`, `ItemDetailsProvider`, `StructureCoreExtension`, `AttributeDescriptor`, `GeneratorDescriptor`, `EffectorDescriptor`) must work when called as `Base.call(this, options)` on an object whose prototype derives from it, not only with `new`.

These AMD ids are public and each resolves directly to the value it names, not to an object with a `default` member: `structure/api/Column`, `structure/api/ColumnConfigurator`, `structure/api/ColumnType`, `structure/api/ColumnGroup`, `structure/api/SpecOption`, `structure/api/AttributeDescriptor`, `structure/api/GeneratorDescriptor`, `structure/api/EffectorDescriptor`, `structure/api/AutomationRegistry`, `structure/api/ItemDetailsProvider`, `structure/api/ItemDetailsBridge`, `structure/api/SecondaryPanelRegistry`, `structure/api/StructureCoreExtension`, `structure/api/StructureCoreExtensionRegistry`. The global does not carry `AttributeDescriptor`, `GeneratorDescriptor`, `EffectorDescriptor`, `ItemDetailsBridge`, `SecondaryPanelRegistry` or `StructureCoreExtension`: those are reached by AMD id only.

The global is created by the widget's own script: a companion script that registers columns or providers must load after `widget-bare` (for example through the web-resource context `structure.widget`). Column types and groups registered that way are visible at once, because all registries are page-wide singletons read on use. `window.namespace(path)` is the plugin's global helper for reaching or creating a dotted object path, and the bundled item-details scripts use it to reach the global.

The jar carries a file of empty placeholder declarations for the global, which no web-resource loads. It names `registerColumn` and `ColumnConfiguratorGroup`, which do not exist on the live global: the live registration calls are `registerColumnType` and `registerColumnGroup`. The replacement does not provide `registerColumn` or `ColumnConfiguratorGroup`. The five browser-side type declaration scripts of the original (effector, progress, details, editor and generic details types) define nothing at run time.

`ColumnType.register(typeOrColumnClass, keys)` (also `registerColumnType`): `keys` is a column key string or a non-empty array of them; anything else throws `expected a non-empty array of column keys, but got <first argument>`. The first argument is either an instance of `ColumnType`, or a subclass of `Column`, which is wrapped in a type whose `createColumn(context, spec)` returns `new columnClass({context, spec})` when `spec.key` is one of `keys` and null otherwise. Anything else throws `expected subclass of ColumnType, but got <value>`. Each key maps to the type; a later registration of a key replaces the earlier mapping, while the earlier type stays in the list of all types.

`ColumnType.getAllColumnTypes()` returns a copy of the registered types in registration order, `ColumnType.getAllColumnTypeKeys()` all keys, and `ColumnType.getColumnTypeForKey(key)` the type for a key or undefined. A column spec whose key has no type yields no column and logs the warning that no column type is registered.

A `ColumnType` instance has these overridable methods with these defaults: `createSwitchTypePreset(context)` null, `createAddColumnPresets(context)` an empty array, `createConfigurator(context, spec)` null, `createColumn(context, spec)` null, `getMetadataRequests(context)`, `getPresetMetadataRequests()`, `getColumnMetadataRequests()` and `getConfigMetadataRequests()` all null.

For each column spec of a view, with a `csid`: an existing column with that csid is reused when its key matches and its spec is deep-equal. Otherwise the type's metadata for the phase `column` is loaded, `createColumn(context, spec)` is called with a copy of the panel's column context extended with that metadata, and then the column's own `getMetadataRequests()` is loaded and added to `column.context`. A null result means no column; the load never fails the view.

When the add-column list opens, for every registered type the phase `preset` metadata is loaded and `createAddColumnPresets(context)` is called with the metadata-extended context; each returned spec gets a configurator. When the edit panel opens with type switching allowed, every other type gets `createSwitchTypePreset(context)` likewise. A non-null spec gets the edited column's `csid` and a configurator through `createConfigurator`. A type returning null is left out of the Type selector.

Metadata requests are a map from a name to a request object. A request with `promise` uses that promise. Otherwise it needs `url` and is sent as an AJAX call with its own settings, `dataType` defaulting to `json`. With `cacheable: true` the promise is kept per url for the page, so the call is made once. `extract(response)`, when a function, turns the answer into the stored value. The result maps each name to its value. A request that fails, or has neither promise nor url, simply leaves its name out and never fails the whole load; an empty or null map resolves to an empty result at once.

A type's metadata is cached on the type, per phase. `getMetadataRequests(context)` is loaded once and applies to all phases; the phases `preset`, `column` and `config` load `getPresetMetadataRequests()`, `getColumnMetadataRequests()` and `getConfigMetadataRequests()` once each. The two results are merged, the phase's values winning. The result is available to the type's create methods through `context.getMetadata(name)`, which falls back to any earlier `getMetadata`; names not found give undefined.

The column context passed to types, columns and configurators has: `jira.getAllIssueFields()` (a copy of all Jira fields), `jira.getIssueFieldById(id)`, `getMetadata(name)`, `isConfigurationPanelResizeAllowed()` (true on a project page or the structure board) and `structure` with `isPrimaryPanel()`, `isSecondaryPanel()`, `isIssuePage()`, `isGreenHopperTab()`, `isPCVPage()`, `isProjectPage()` (the last two the same answer), `isComponentPage()` and `isVersionPage()` (always false), `isGadget()`, `isLocalGadget()`, `isRemoteGadget()`, `isStructureBoard()`, `isConfluenceEnabled()` and `onExternalParametersChanged()`, which makes the panel treat its columns as changed so that they re-render.

`new Column({spec, context?, csid?})` needs a spec. `csid` is `spec.csid` or else the option; with neither it throws `cannot create column without csid`. `options`, `spec`, `context` and `csid` are kept on the instance. `spec.name`, when set, is rendered as a template with `{column: this}` to give the display name: braces in it are substituted.

On `Column`: `getColumnSpec()` returns the spec, `getCsid()` the csid, `getColumnKey()` `spec.key`, `isColumnOfType(key)` compares keys, `getName()` is the rendered name or else `getDefaultName()` or else the empty string, and `getDefaultName()` is empty.

`Column` defaults: `isUniversal()` false, `isResizable()` true, `canShrinkWhenNoSpace()` false, `isAutoSizeAllowed()` false, `isRenderingAbsentValueAllowed()` true, `getMinWidth()` 27, `getDefaultWidth()` 120, `getSortAttribute()` null, `isSortDescendingByDefault()` false, `getMetadataRequests()` null, `getSuggestedAttributeSpecs()` null, `getCellValueHtml(context)` the empty string, `collectRequiredAttributes(set)` and `updateRowClasses(context)` do nothing.

`Column.setWidth(w)`: an empty w clears the manual width (`getWidth()` gives null); otherwise the stored width is the larger of w as an integer and `getMinWidth()`. So with the default minimum, setWidth(10) gives 27 and setWidth(200) gives 200. When a view is restored, manual widths are applied through `setWidth`, and preferred widths only to columns with `isAutoSizeAllowed()` true. A column's initial width is `getDefaultWidth()`, or the minimum width if that is 0. `isResizable()` false gives the column no drag handle, and it takes no part in width distribution. `canShrinkWhenNoSpace()` true lets the column go below its width when the grid lacks room.

`Column.renderHeader(cell)` sets the header cell's HTML to `getHeaderCellHtml()`, which is the column's name in the standard header layout, or the empty string when the name is empty. The name is inserted as HTML, unescaped by this step.

For each row on screen and each column, the grid calls `column.render(context)`. The default `render` calls `renderCellView(context)`: it gets `getCellViewHtml(context)`, replaces the cell's HTML only if it differs, and then calls `updateRowClasses(context)`. `getCellViewHtml` wraps `getCellValueHtml(context)` through `wrapInCellDiv(html, extraClass = "")`, the standard cell layout with the fade and the overflow indicator. An exception from `render` logs a warning and empties that cell; other cells still render.

The render context offers: `getRowId()`, `getItemId()`, `getMeta()`, `getSemantics()`, `isIssue()`, `isNotAccessible()`, `getAttributeValue(attributeSpec, forestSpec?)` and `repaintWhen(promise)`, which re-renders the row when a still pending promise ends and does nothing for a settled one. `forestSpec` is omitted or `displayed` for the shown forest, or `unfiltered`. `getAttributeValue` returns undefined for a value not loaded. The cell and row elements are at `context._cell$` and `context._row$`, valid only during the `render` call; a column overriding `render` writes to them directly.

When a `render` call read at least one attribute and every value read was absent, the row is accessible and `isRenderingAbsentValueAllowed()` is true, the grid replaces the cell with its absent-value display. A row whose data has not arrived yet is not rendered at all: its cells get the same display, under the same two conditions. If a value read is known to be outdated, the cell is marked as outdated. Returning false from `isRenderingAbsentValueAllowed()` means the column's own output stays.

Whenever the panel's columns change, `collectRequiredAttributes(set)` is called on each column, with `set.requireAttribute(attributeSpec, forestSpec?)` to declare what it needs. The union is what the grid subscribes to and what `getAttributeValue` can return. An exception logs an error and that column contributes what it declared before the exception.

`Column.shouldFlash(flashContext)`: true if any attribute declared through `collectRequiredAttributes` is flashed according to `flashContext.isAttributeFlashed(attributeSpec, forestSpec)`. When true the grid plays the changed-value flash on the cell. An exception from it is logged and means no flash.

`getSortTransform()` gives, when `getSortAttribute()` returns an attribute spec, `{module: "com.almworks.jira.structure:sorter-attribute", params: {attribute: <spec>}}`, otherwise null. A null transform means clicking the column's header does not sort. It may also return a promise of the transform. On the first sort by this column the sort is descending exactly when `isSortDescendingByDefault()` is true; clicking the same sort again reverses the direction.
`getSuggestedAttributeSpecs()`, when it returns specs, offers them in every attribute selector of the widget under Used in Columns, named after the column.

`Column.safeSetHtml(element, html)` sets the HTML of a non-empty element and never lets an exception out. On an exception it logs one warning per column name for the page's life, with the column's name, spec, the cell HTML and the error's stack. An empty or missing element is ignored. The warning names no vendor and sends nothing anywhere.

`new ColumnConfigurator({spec, context?})` needs a spec. It takes `presetName`, `description` and `groupKey` out of the spec, when they are set, into the configurator, so they never reach the saved column spec. `getContext()` returns the context, `shareSpec()` the spec itself (not a copy), and `getColumnSpec()` the same spec.

`getPresetName()` is the taken `presetName` or else `getColumnName()`; `getColumnName()` is `spec.name`, or else `getDefaultColumnName()`, or else `getColumnTypeName()`. `getDefaultColumnName()`, `getColumnTypeName()` and `getColumnTypeInfoLink()` default to the empty string, `getDescription()` to the taken description or the empty string, `getGroupKey()` to the taken key or false.

`ColumnConfigurator` defaults: `getOptions()` false (no custom options), `isConfigured()` true, `getMetadataRequests()` null, `isConfigurationPanelWide()` false, `isConfigurationPanelResizable()` false. `isConfigurationRevertible(originalSpec)` is true when the current spec is not deep-equal to originalSpec. `matchPreset(spec)` compares `comparablePreset(spec)` with `comparablePreset` of its own spec, and by default `comparablePreset` keeps only `key`.

In the add-column list each configurator is one entry, named by `getPresetName()`, with `getDescription()` as its tooltip. Entries are sorted by the rendered name and placed under the group with `getGroupKey()`; an entry with no key, or a key of no registered group, goes under the group with an empty key, and with no such group it is not listed. Choosing an entry adds `getColumnSpec()` when `isConfigured()` is true and otherwise just closes the list, adding nothing.

A configurator is obtained by loading the phase `config` metadata, calling `createConfigurator(context, spec)` with the extended context, and then loading the configurator's own `getMetadataRequests()` into `configurator.context`. Failure at any step gives no configurator, never an error.

`ColumnGroup.register(options)` (also `registerColumnGroup`) adds a group of the add-column list. Options: `groupKey` (a string, otherwise it throws `no valid groupKey`), `title` (non-empty, otherwise `no title`) and `order` (a number, default 0, otherwise `bad order type`). A missing or non-object argument throws `bad options object`. `ColumnGroup.getGroups()` returns a copy in registration order; instances have `getGroupKey()`, `getTitle()`, `getOrder()`.

In the add-column list groups are sorted by `order` ascending, then by rendered title. A title may hold `{message.key}` placeholders, which are replaced by message text when shown. The widget itself registers the group `pages`, titled from the message `sw.conf.colsec.pages`, with order 500. A group with no entries is not listed.

`new SpecOption(options)` reads: `configurator`, `context` (else `configurator.getContext()`, else an empty object), `spec` (else `configurator.shareSpec()`, else an empty object), `title` (default the empty string), `getValue`, `setValue`, `param`, `defaultValue` and the function-valued `fieldGroupClass` and `onOptionNotify`, which replace the methods of those names. All options stay available as `this.options`. With no argument nothing is set.

Default `getValue()` reads `spec.params[param]` and gives `defaultValue` when that is undefined or null. Default `setValue(v)`: when v equals `defaultValue` (strictly) it deletes the param and, if `spec.params` is then empty, deletes `params`; otherwise it creates `params` if needed and stores v; then it triggers the `notify` event on the option's row, if the row exists. Both throw `no spec` without a spec and `no param` without a param.

`createRow()` makes a field group whose extra class is `fieldGroupClass()` (default empty), calls `createLabel(row)` (default: a label with the title text) and `createInput(row)` (default: nothing), stores the row as `div$` and returns it. The host keeps the option on the row, and adds it to the form in the order the options were given.

Any `notify` event from an option's row reaches the host form, optionally with a reason. The host calls `notify(reason)` on every option except the one that fired, in reverse row order; a truthy answer shows that row and a falsy one hides it; then `isInputValid()` is read. The reasons are `prepare` before the panel appears, `show` right after, `update` for ordinary changes (the default) and `close` when the panel leaves that configurator. Default `notify` returns `onOptionNotify()`, which defaults to true, and default `isInputValid()` is true.

`getReadinessPromise()` defaults to a resolved promise. An option with work still pending returns a pending one. Before the edit column panel hides, and before a form with an attribute selector submits, the host waits for all options' promises, for 2000 ms at most: on a rejection or the timeout it goes on regardless.
`SpecOption` carries the option classes as statics: `SpecOption.Attribute`, `.Checkbox`, `.Aggregate`, `.Text`, `.Select`, `.Toggle`.

`SpecOption.Checkbox` shows a checkbox with `title` as its own label, with no separate field label unless a `createLabel` option is given. A `template` option may replace the layout; it must contain a checkbox input. Its value starts from `getValue()` at construction (so it needs the spec and param, or a custom getter), and each change calls `setValue`. `notify` re-reads `getValue()` and then answers as the base class does. `isInputValid()` is always true.

`SpecOption.Text` shows a text input, or the first input of a `template` option when one is given. Typing calls `setValue` with the text; `notify` re-reads `getValue()` and always returns true, without calling `onOptionNotify`. `isInputValid()` is always true.

`SpecOption.Select` needs an `options` option, otherwise it throws `no options`. That is an array, a promise, or a function called with the row (this being the option) that returns either; entries are `{value, name}`, nested arrays are flattened, and entries with an undefined `value` or empty `name` are dropped. The select is hidden until the entries load, with a spinner when that takes over 500 ms. Then it becomes a Jira single-select, showing `getValue()`, and each truthy new choice calls `setValue` and fires `notify`. `notify` sets the current value and returns true; `isInputValid()` is true when a value is chosen.

`SpecOption.Toggle` needs a `template` option holding an AUI toggle element. The value starts from `getValue()` and each change calls `setValue`, and then the `onToggleChange(value)` option if given. `notify("show")` calls the `onToggleShow(container)` option, then it answers as the base class does. `updateToggle()` sets the value to the opposite of the element's checked state.

`SpecOption.Attribute` needs `getValue` and `setValue` options, otherwise it throws `no getter` or `no setter`. Its input is a text area holding the attribute spec as JSON (`{}` when there is none), turned into the attribute selector at the first `notify`, with the options `expectedFormat`, `presetFilter`, `usePrimaryFormat` and the context. A later edit that parses as JSON with an `id` calls `setValue` and fires `notify`, as does the selector changing size. `notify("close")`, after the first, stores the choice in the recent list. `notify` always returns true. `isInputValid()` is true when the text parses as JSON.

`SpecOption.Aggregate` shows three checkboxes, in this order: Sum over sub-items, Exclude duplicates, After filtering. The last two are shown only while the first is on. Each change calls its `setValue` with null when the sum is off, or with `{forestSpec, distinct}`, where `forestSpec` is `displayed` when After filtering is on and `unfiltered` when not, and fires `notify`.

`SpecOption.Aggregate` defaults: `getValue` returns `spec.params`. `setValue(null)` deletes `aggregate`, `forestSpec` and `distinct` from `params`; `setValue(v)` stores `aggregate: "sum"`, `forestSpec` (any value other than `displayed` or `unfiltered` logs a warning and counts as `displayed`; an empty one without the warning) and `distinct` as a boolean. Nothing is stored when `spec.params` is absent. The checkboxes read as on when the value's `aggregate` is `sum`; After filtering is on when `forestSpec` is `displayed` or empty.

`SpecOption.Aggregate` default `isApplicable()`: the Jira field named by `spec.params.field` is summable: it is `worklogged`, a system field of type duration or number, or a numeric custom field that is not on the widget's excluded list. `notify`, when applicable, refreshes the checkboxes and returns true. When not applicable it unticks them, deletes `aggregate`, `forestSpec` and `distinct` from `params` and returns false, which hides the row.

The widget's radio-group option (not part of the public surface) shows one radio per `{value, label}`, named after `param`. A change stores the chosen value under `spec.params.view`, creating `params` if needed, and fires `notify`; `notify` selects `spec.params.view` or else `defaultValue`. It is used by the user field column for its display choice and that column hides it unless the field is a user field. The parameter name `view` is fixed, whatever `param` says (as the original does).

`registerCoreExtension({key, extension})` (global, and on `structure/api/StructureCoreExtensionRegistry`) stores the extension under `key`, which is the complete key of the server's `structure-core-extension` module. An argument without `key` or `extension` is silently ignored; a later registration under the same key replaces the former one.

`StructureCoreExtension` is a base class with `getExtensionRequest()` (default null) and `isBlockingPoll()` (default false). Registered extensions must have both of these; `isBlockingSubscriptionUpload()` is optional.

At every `POST /rest/structure/2.0/poll` the widget calls `getExtensionRequest()` of each extension. A truthy answer goes in the body's `extensionRequests` map under the extension's key; with no answers the field is left out. An extension that throws logs an error and is skipped; the others still go.

`structure/api/StructureCoreExtensionRegistry` has, besides `registerCoreExtension`: `getExtensionRequests()` (the map described for polling), `isPollBlocked()` (true when any extension's `isBlockingPoll()` is true) and `isSubscriptionUploadBlocked()` (true when any extension has a function `isBlockingSubscriptionUpload` and it answers true).

While `isBlockingPoll()` of any extension is true, automatic polls are not sent, and the answer to an automatic poll that arrives meanwhile is dropped unprocessed. While `isBlockingSubscriptionUpload()` of any extension is true, the widget's value subscription is not created, updated or deleted on the server; that resumes at the next upload attempt once it is no longer blocked.

The widget tracks user activity. It counts as active from load. A mouse press or key press anywhere on the page, a window resize or scroll, a scroll of the grid, or the window or an embedded frame gaining focus all count as activity, unless the widget is reported as not displayed. Every 2 seconds, if the last activity is over 300000 ms (5 minutes) ago, it turns inactive and tells the widget; the next activity turns it active and tells the widget again. With a threshold of 0 or less the check never runs, and it stays active. The polling owner uses this to slow down.

`structure/api/AutomationRegistry` (the global's `automationRegistry`) has `registerGeneratorFactory(factory)` and `registerEffectorFactory(factory)`. Both add to one page-wide queue. Each factory is called once, with `{widget, addDescriptor}`, the first time a label for a generator or a name for an effector is requested after it was queued; factories queued later run at the next such request. Registered factories are applied to the first widget that asks.

`addDescriptor(descriptor)` ignores an empty argument and files the descriptor under its `moduleKey`, the complete module key of the generator or effector: an instance of `GeneratorDescriptor` as a generator, of `EffectorDescriptor` as an effector. A missing `moduleKey` throws `invalid module key <key>`, another class throws `Unsupported descriptor superclass for module "<key>".` and a generator `moduleKey` already filed throws `Descriptor for module "<key>" is already registered`. A second effector with the same key is not caught and replaces the first (as the original does).

`new GeneratorDescriptor({moduleKey})` stores `moduleKey`. `suggestLabel(spec)` defaults to null. It is called with `{module, params}` for a generator that matches no catalogue preset, to label it in the transformations UI; it returns a string or a promise of one. A label from a matching preset wins over the descriptor; a generator with neither gets no label.

`new EffectorDescriptor({moduleKey})` stores `moduleKey`. `generateName(template, formParams)` must be overridden: the default throws `Unsupported operation "generateName" for module "<key>"`. It is called while the user edits an effector, with the catalogue's name template and the form's values, and returns a string or a promise of one. When the module has no descriptor, or the template or params are missing, no name is produced. `styleParam(value)` returns value, unescaped, wrapped in the same highlighted parameter span that the server's automation summaries use.

The server's generator and effector summaries may hold elements carrying a `data-attribute-spec` attribute (JSON), with a parameter span containing `{attribute}`. Before they are shown, that placeholder is replaced by the HTML-escaped label of the attribute, as the attribute registry suggests it. Until the attribute metadata is loaded the text reads Attribute, and the row is repainted when it is. A summary with no such element is returned unchanged.

Per widget, the transformer kinds are looked up by key: filter, sorter, grouper, extender and group, each present once. The legacy transformation keys `unresolved` and `assigned2me` count as filters. Whether a transformation is a filter or a sorter is decided by the type of its generator in the automation catalogue, found by its module key, which may be given alone or as `module` of an object; an unknown module is neither.

`registerItemDetailsProvider(itemType, providerClass)`: `itemType` is a complete item type key such as `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`. Registration waits until the details panel has started. It then creates `new providerClass({widget, itemDetailsBridge})` and adds its `viewport` to the details panel, active only while the current row has that item type. A non-string type throws `Invalid item type "<type>"`; a class not derived from `ItemDetailsProvider` throws `Details provider class must be a subclass of ItemDetailsProvider`. A provider with no function `showDetails` or a `viewport` that is not a DOM element logs and throws an error beginning `Failed to register ItemDetailsProvider`. Registering a type again replaces the provider with a warning. The plugin's scripts register providers for the issue, memo and planning task types; any other type is a companion's.

`ItemDetailsProvider` has `widget` and `itemDetailsBridge` set at construction, and defaults: `viewport` null, `extendFocusedRowData(row)` a resolved deferred of row, `showDetails()` throws `showDetails is not implemented for item details provider`, `beforeHide()` and `cancelUnfinishedEdits()` nothing, `hasUnfinishedEdits()` false, `timeoutMessageKey` `timeout`, `panelClass` the empty string, `applyWidth()` nothing, `focusElementClass` `detailsFocusElement`, `onDetailsFocusing()` nothing, `refreshDetails(row)` a resolved deferred of row, `refreshOnStructureUpdate` false, `setDebug()` nothing.

When the focused row changes on the focused panel, `extendFocusedRowData({rowId, itemId, itemType, panel})` of the type's provider is called and must return a jQuery deferred, resolved with the row data the provider wants (it should keep those four fields). If pending, the panel shows the stub state at once; after 1000 ms the host itself rejects the deferred with `timeoutMessageKey`. A rejection `(messageKey, isError)` shows the stub for that key, as an error when isError is true. When the row is left the deferred is rejected with nothing.

`showDetails(rowData, life)` is called when the details panel is on and the current row changed, debounced by 500 ms, and when the panel is turned on. It returns a deferred. While the row is the same item as the one already loaded, it is not called again. Resolving marks the item loaded, rejecting with `(messageKey, isError)` shows the stub, and the host rejects the deferred itself when `life` ends. `beforeHide(rowData)` is called once when the panel, having been shown, is turned off.

The panel's header shows `getHeaderTitle(rowData)`; the default is the row's summary from `rowData.panel`, or Item Details if empty. Its icon is `getIcon(rowData)`, an HTML string or a promise of one; the default promises the row's `icon` attribute in `html` format. With no row, an information icon is shown.

`panelClass` is added to the details panel while the current row's type uses this provider. `applyWidth(width)` is called with the panel's width when the current item type changes and when the width changes, in either case once the panel can be interacted with. When focus moves to the details, the visible element with class `focusElementClass` gets it, or else the `viewport`, and then `onDetailsFocusing()` is called.

`refreshDetails(rowData, life)` returns a deferred. It runs 800 ms after a refresh is asked for, at most one pending per item, and only if the same item is still current in an enabled panel. On success the header is refreshed. With `refreshOnStructureUpdate` true a refresh is also asked for when a poll's item update is full or names the current item; the panel stays interactive meanwhile.

Before the details panel is turned off or the row is left, 100 ms after the attempt, `hasUnfinishedEdits(rowData)` is asked. If true a confirmation dialog asks: You have some unfinished edits on the details page. Leave it without applying changes? Confirming calls `cancelUnfinishedEdits(rowData)` and leaves. Declining puts focus back where it was, calls `onDetailsFocusing()` and stays.

`ItemDetailsBridge` (the `itemDetailsBridge` given to a provider; constructed by the host only) has: `panel$`, the details panel element; `getCurrentRowData()`, the current row data when its item type is the provider's, otherwise null; `onCurrentRowChange(fn)`, calling fn with that value at once and at each change; `toggleEnabled(on?)`, with no boolean flipping the panel, and turning off subject to the unfinished-edits check; `onEnableToggling(fn)`, called at once and at each change; `isEnabled()`; `isVisible()`; `whenVisible(fn)`, called once when the panel can be interacted with; `onDetachment(fn)`, called when the details panel is destroyed.

`ItemDetailsBridge` focus members: `isFocused()` (on and focused), `setFocused(on)` (acts only if the panel is on and visible; false blurs), `notifyFocusChanged(on)`, `onFocusChange(fn)` (at once and at each change), and `focusStealerStarts(id, isFocusedNow?)` and `focusStealerFinishes(id, preventFocusing?)`. A stealer that starts while details are focused (or with isFocusedNow true, or when others are already recorded) is recorded; when the last recorded one finishes without preventFocusing, focus returns to the details as soon as they can be interacted with. `shouldBlockActions()` is true when the panel was shown but cannot be interacted with now.

`notifyDetailsEditStarted()` and `notifyDetailsEditStopped()` tell the widget that an edit in the details started or stopped. `notifyDetailsUpdated()` tells it the edit stopped and the item may have changed, so the grid refreshes it.

`requestRefreshDetails(deferred, itemId, keepInteractive)`: when itemId is given and is not the current item, deferred resolves at once. Otherwise details are refreshed as `refreshDetails` describes, the deferred resolves when that ends, whatever its result, and `notifyDetailsUpdated` applies. With keepInteractive false and the refresh still pending, the panel is shown as loading until it ends.

`updateItemData(values)` returns a deferred, rejected at once when there is no current item or panel. Otherwise the update joins the widget's upload queue: `POST /rest/structure/2.0/item/update` with body `{item: {itemId, values}, items: {version}, forest: {spec, version}}`, where `itemId` is complete. A newer update of the same item replaces one not yet sent. A failed upload rejects the deferred. An answer with `success` true first refreshes the details, then resolves with the answer; with `success` false it resolves with the answer, whose fields are `success`, `successfulActions`, `formErrors` and `fieldErrors`.

`structure/api/SecondaryPanelRegistry.registerSecondaryPanel(layoutName, descriptor)` waits until the widget is ready, appends `descriptor.panel$` to it and records the panel. With no widget on the page it does nothing. A name already registered is an assertion failure. `onRegisterPanel(fn)` calls `fn(layoutName, descriptor)` once for each panel, those already present and those to come. `getPanelDescriptors()` returns all descriptors.

A registered panel adds a layout named `layoutName`. It adds an entry to the layout menu, labelled `descriptor.menuItemText` or else the name, and the action `layout.<layoutName>`, titled by `descriptor.toggleActionText`. It gets the shortcuts ctrl+alt+N and ctrl+alt+num_N, where N starts at 5 and rises by one per registered panel, in registration order. When the current layout has this name, the panel is shown at once.

The descriptor's other fields: `defaultWidth` and `minWidth` (numbers, required for sizing), `isPerspectiveReady()` and `writePerspectiveSpec(spec, write)` (required; called when the perspective is saved, and it writes only when ready), and these optional ones: `start()` (once, at first show), `afterShown()`, `afterHide()`, `onResize`, `focusPanel`, `tabFocusPanel`, `updateVertical`, `useTransferFocus`, `horizontalSplitter$`, `controlCell`, `isComponentVisible(component)`, `icon` (the toolbar's layout icon), `titleText` (added to the browser title after ` | ` while shown) and `key` (the companion app's key).

After showing a registered panel, the widget reads the `extensions` entry for `descriptor.key` in the widget configuration, which the companion app supplies. When that entry's `licensed` is not true, the layout goes back to the previous one, or else to `single`. The flag is the companion app's own setting: the plugin neither computes nor checks it. Any other layout name has no panel, and the secondary panel is hidden.

`new AttributeDescriptor({id, label, formats})` stores id and label as strings, and formats, either an array (frozen) or `*`. `getAttributeID()` and `getLabel()` throw `invalid descriptor, ID is not defined` and `invalid descriptor, no label` when unset. Defaults: `suggestLabel()` is `getLabel()`, `createOptions()` an empty array, `getDefaultSpec()` `{id}`, `isConfigurable()` false, `isParamsValid()` true, `getSupportedFormats()` the formats or `*`.

`isFormatSupported(f)` is true when the supported formats are `*` or include f; `isFormatSupportedBySpec(spec, f)` defaults to that; `getPrimaryFormat()` is the first format, or null with none or `*`. `AttributeDescriptor.Formats` is a frozen `{ALL: "*", BASIC: ["html"], NUMERIC: ["number"]}`. The format names used across the widget are `html`, `text`, `number`, `order`, `duration`, `time` and `any`.
`suggestName(columnName, spec)`: when columnName equals `suggestLabel(spec)` the answer is columnName, otherwise it reads `<columnName> (<label>)`.

Attribute descriptors are registered per widget through page-wide factories of the attribute registry: there is no member of the global or of `structure/api/` to add one. The widget adds its own in this way, and `structure/api/AttributeDescriptor` is public as a base class only.

Each widget has one attribute registry, filled once, on first need, by page-wide factories, each of which may add attributes and named presets and may work asynchronously. A factory that throws, or whose asynchronous work fails, is logged and the others go on. When all have ended the set is fixed: nothing can be added later. Asking for an attribute or for presets before that is an error. A standalone registry can also be made for pages with no widget, with its own connection to the server.

Adding an attribute with an empty id, or an id already present, is an error (`descriptor with ID "<id>" is already registered`). A preset is a name with a spec, which is normalised to its `id` and non-empty `params`, all else dropped; a preset whose normalised spec is already there is ignored.

The registry's answers: asking for an unknown attribute is an error (`unknown attribute ID "<id>"`). Presets can be listed all together or for one format, meaning those whose spec supports it. The label of a spec is the name of the preset with that normalised spec, else the descriptor's `suggestLabel`, else none. Whether a spec supports a format: no for no spec, yes for no format, no for an unknown id, else the descriptor's answer. Whether a spec is valid: no without an id; for an unknown id yes in the lenient sense and no in the strict sense; else the descriptor's `isParamsValid(spec.params)`. The primary format of a spec is the descriptor's answer, or `text`.

The attribute `count` is labelled Count Sub-Items, in formats number, text, html and order, and is configurable. Its single option, the checkbox Leaves Only, stores `params.leaves: true` when on and deletes it when off. With `leaves` set the label is Count Leaves.

The attribute `customfield` covers Jira custom fields whose id is `customfield_<positive number>`. Its option Custom Field is a select of those fields, limited to those supporting the expected format and passing the selector's filter; it stores `params.fieldId` as the number. Its label is the field's name. Format support: html, order, text and no format for every field; number for type `number`; time for `date` and `datetime`. Primary format: number for `number`, time for dates, text for `string`, none otherwise. It is valid when `fieldId` is a known field. An unknown field supports only the request for no format.

The attribute `formatted-number` is labelled Formatted Number, in formats text and html, and is not configurable. It is valid when `params.attribute.format` is `number`, `time` or `duration`, and `params.type` is `number`, `percentage`, `datetime` or `duration`. For a source attribute labelled S, the label is `S (as text)`, and the name from a column C is `C (S (as text))` unless S equals C, when it is `C (as text)`.

The attribute `expr` is labelled Formula..., in formats number, text, html, duration, time, order and any, with primary format any, and is configurable. It is valid when `params.formula` is non-empty. Its one option is the formula editor, bound to `params.formula` and `params.variables`. Default spec, label and name come from the formula column's rules.
The attribute `links-count` is labelled Links count, in format number only, and is not configurable.

The query match attribute takes its id, default spec, options, label and name from the query match column, is labelled Query match..., in formats number, text and html, with primary format number, and is configurable. It is valid when `params.query` and `params.queryType` are both non-empty. Option values live in `params`, an empty value being stored as the empty string.

The attribute `sum` is labelled Sum..., in formats number, duration, text, html and order, and is configurable. It is valid when `params.attribute.format` is `number`, `duration` or `any`. Options: the attribute selector Attribute to Sum, stored in `params.attribute` and offering only other attributes than sum whose primary format is number or duration (and customizable entries); and the checkbox Exclude Duplicates, stored as `params.distinct: true`, deleted when off.

For sum, with a summed attribute labelled S, the label is `Σ S`, and `Σ! S` with `distinct`. With an unlabelled summed attribute the label is Sum..., and with none it is null. The name from a column C is `C (Σ S)` (or with `Σ!`) unless `Σ S` equals C, or S has no label, when it is C. The primary format is that of the summed attribute when number or duration, otherwise number.

With Tempo's planning API present, the attribute of the Tempo planned time column is added, labelled Tempo Planned Time..., in formats duration, text, html and order, and configurable, with the column's default spec and label. Options, in order: date from, date to, a user picker (or a plain user input when the current user lacks the picker permission or the widget is a remote gadget), team, team role. Values live in `params` under each option's param, and are written only while the spec's id is this attribute's. Without Tempo the attribute does not exist.

With Tempo Timesheets present, the attribute of the Tempo work logged column is added, labelled Tempo Work Logged..., in formats duration, text, html and order, and configurable, with the column's default spec and label. Options, in order: date from, date to, account, a user picker (or plain input, under the same condition as for planned time), team, and a checkbox in the column's billable layout stored as `params.billable`. Without Tempo the attribute does not exist.

The time in status attribute takes id, default spec, options and label from the time in status column, is labelled Time in Status..., in formats duration, number, text, html and order, with primary format duration, and is configurable. It is valid when `params.statuses` is non-empty.

The attribute `transition-date` is labelled Transition Date..., in formats time, order, text, number and html, and is configurable. Its params: `status` or `category` (a non-empty string, `status` winning) and `transition` (`first` or `latest`, anything else counting as `latest`). It is valid when either a status or a category is set. Options: the select Status, listing `Category: <name>` for each status category and then `Status: <name>` for each status (values `category:<id>` and `status:<id>`; choosing one deletes the other param); and the select Transition with Latest transition to status and First transition to status.

The label of `transition-date` is `First Transition to Status "<name>"`, `Latest Transition to Status "<name>"`, `First Transition to <category>` or `Latest Transition to <category>`, by the transition and qualifier; a name not in the status configuration is shown as its id. With no qualifier it is Transition Date. It adds two presets when those status categories exist: First Transition to the category `indeterminate` and Latest Transition to the category `done`.

The attribute `user-property` is labelled User Property..., in formats text, html and order, and is configurable. It is valid when `params.userKey` and `params.propertyName` are set. Options: the attribute selector User Field, stored in `params.userKey`, in format text, offering only Jira fields of type user or arrays of users (and customizable entries); and the text field Property, stored in `params.propertyName`. Its label is `<user field>[<property>]`, or User Property when one of them is missing, or null with no user field.

The attribute selector (also the input of `SpecOption.Attribute`) decorates a text area whose value is the JSON spec; on any other element it fails, and a second selector on the same text area is the first one. Its settings: the expected format (default `html`), or to use each attribute's primary format instead; a filter on specs; which groups to offer (default all but None); the text of the None entry (default None); the column being edited, left out of Used in Columns; and whether to hide the manual text area. Plugin templates may state the expected format in the markup; a page's form with a selector behaves the same with either.

The selector shows a single-select, with a Configure toggle button beside it only when the selection is configurable. Below sit the descriptor's options, shown while Configure is on, and the Specification text area, shown only for Manual Specification. While metadata loads the select is hidden, with a spinner after 500 ms.

The select lists, in order: the placeholder Select attribute..., the group Customized (the current spec when it matches no entry but has a label), the None entry when asked for, whose spec is `{id: "-none-"}`, then Recently Used, Used in Columns, Standard Attributes, Customizable Attribute, and Advanced with Manual Specification. A group with no entries is not offered. `presetFilter`, when given, applies to all groups but Manual and None; for a Customizable Attribute entry it sees the spec with `configure: true`.

Used in Columns lists, over all panels, the `getSuggestedAttributeSpecs()` of every column except the one being edited, each distinct spec once, if it supports the format and is valid in the strict sense, named by the descriptor's `suggestName(columnName, spec)`. Standard Attributes lists the registry's presets for the format. Customizable Attribute lists configurable descriptors that support the format, by `getLabel()`, and choosing one opens its options. All but Recently Used are sorted by name, ignoring case.

Recently Used shows up to 3 specs that fit the format and have a label, latest first. Only a top-level selector records, never one nested in another's options: at its form's submit, or when its option is closed, a valid spec (strict) goes to the front. The list keeps 3 distinct specs, shared by all selectors, and stays in the browser across sessions, per browser and not per Jira user.

Showing a given spec: one with an empty id selects nothing, or None when None is offered; one with a `format` of its own selects Manual Specification; one matching an entry selects it; one the registry can label appears as a single entry under Customized; anything else selects Manual Specification. The Customized entry goes away 50 ms after another entry is chosen.

The text area always holds the spec with a `format`: the expected format or, with `usePrimaryFormat`, the attribute's primary format (`text` with no id). With nothing chosen it holds `{"id": "", "format": ...}` or the None id. On reading, a `format` equal to the expected one is dropped from the internal spec, so a manually typed different format is kept.

Choosing a configurable entry keeps Configure off unless the entry came from Customizable Attribute. Pressing Configure shows the options of that attribute's descriptor (`createOptions(context)`), and releasing it hides them, returning to the matching entry. Choosing another attribute replaces the options.

`createOptions(context)` gets the column context plus `getSpec()` (a deep copy of the current spec), `updateSpec(fn, thisArg?)`, `getExpectedFormat()` and `getSpecFilter()`. `updateSpec` calls fn with a copy: returning false or null drops the change; an object replaces the spec; otherwise the changed copy is stored. A change of `id` is refused with a warning.

The selector's other abilities: it can load a new spec, staying in configure mode if on; it can be disabled, which disables inputs and buttons, makes text read-only and greyed out, and hides the formula controls; it can take focus once loaded. Its size changes are checked at most every 200 ms during mouse moves over the text area, and at each mouse release.
At its form's submit, if the descriptor options are not all ready, the submit is cancelled and repeated once they are or after 2000 ms, with a flag so the second one passes.

The column editing panel opens from a column header's configure control, under the column, on the column's right unless there is no room. Only one is open on the page; opening another closes the first. The type selector and Remove are left out for the main column (key `main`), where also the button row shows only when revert is possible. Otherwise the panel loads a configurator for the column and one per other type that offers a switch preset. If the column's type is unknown or gives no configurator, the panel does not open.

Top to bottom the panel holds: Name, then Type (a select of type names, sorted by name), then the configurator's `getOptions()`. Below are Remove column (tooltip Remove this column), Revert changes (tooltip Revert all changes) and Learn more (tooltip Visit documentation page), which opens the `getColumnTypeInfoLink()` address in a new tab and exists only when the link is non-empty. The form area scrolls above 383 px or the room available. The panel can be resized when the context allows it and `isConfigurationPanelResizable()` is true, and is wider when `isConfigurationPanelWide()` is true.

Every change in the panel is applied live. After each `notify` with no invalid option, a copy of the spec is queued, and 350 ms after the last change it is applied, so the grid updates with the panel still open. With any invalid option nothing is queued, and a spec with no key logs a warning.

Revert changes is visible when any option is invalid or `isConfigurationRevertible(originalSpec)` is true. It reloads the configurator for the column as it was when the panel opened, rebuilds the panel and applies that spec, leaving the panel open. If the reload fails the original spec is applied and the panel closes.

In the panel: Esc applies the pending spec and closes; Enter in any form control, a text area included, does the same, except in a single-select's text field, as does Jira's submit-form shortcut. Enter on Remove column or Revert changes acts as a click; after Revert, focus goes to Remove column. Tab on the last control goes to the first, and Shift+Tab on the first goes to the last. On opening, focus goes to the first input other than the pin button, and it returns on closing.

Choosing another Type applies the `close` notify to the current options, flushes any pending spec and makes that type's configurator current: its Name and options replace the old ones, and its spec is applied like any change. Going back to the first type shows its configurator as it was left.

Remove column removes the column from the view and closes the panel. The same happens when the column is backed by a saved column (`params.savedColumn`) and that saved column is deleted while the panel is open.

Closing the panel waits for options to be ready, for 2000 ms at most, and stops waiting if it is reopened. It then applies the `close` notify, flushes the pending spec and clears it. Clicks in dropdowns, dialogs, the blanket or the page body do not count as clicks outside the panel. Asking for another column while closing finishes the close first.

The Name field holds `getColumnName()`. Typing updates `spec.name` 250 ms after the last key, and an empty field deletes `spec.name`. Leaving an empty field fills in the default name. The option is invalid when `spec.name` is the empty string. A hidden check makes the panel invalid when the spec has no key.

With a horizontally scrollable view, for all but the main column, a toggle with tooltip Pin column sits by the Name label. It shows and sets the pinned state of the column, records `columns.pin` or `columns.unpin` through the statistics, keeps the panel on that column as its position changes, and follows pin changes from elsewhere.

A column that supports inline editing renders the cell editor instead of its view while editing is active and loaded; if the editor has no input yet, the cell shows the view inside the editor's frame. When editing ends the editor is removed, an inline layer left open by it is closed, and the view is drawn. Defaults: the column is editable, is not known to be uneditable for an issue, and creates no editor unless overridden.

A cell with an own and an aggregated value shows the aggregate, followed by the own value in a muted form, with the tooltip This issue's own value is shown in gray. If the two read the same after trimming, or the aggregate is missing, it shows the single value with no tooltip.
